claims.claim_text: Indexed Vincenzon Vacirca is high-confidence matched to Vincenzo Vacirca, a 1942 Voice of America Italian Section employee and early Max Corvo collaborator.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exceptionally rare surname, near-identical given name and coherent 1942 VOA-to-OSS context support the spelling-variant match.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from a rare name and two independent institutional sources linking Vincenzo Vacirca to both the 1942 VOA Italian Section and Max Corvo's OSS circle.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish contemporaneous 1942 employment and OSS collaboration but do not explicitly narrate the transition.
claims.match_notes: Vincenzon remains the indexed spelling; Vincenzo is retained as a documented variant rather than silently substituted.

claims.claim_text: The Voice of America Italian Section within the Office of War Information is Vincenzo Vacirca's best-supported immediate pre-OSS institutional affiliation.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Centro Primo Levi names him among the Italian Section's ten employees in 1942; a separate institutional history identifies him among Max Corvo's earliest collaborators.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence rare-name and wartime institutional match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate affiliation: the two 1942 contexts align, but neither source explicitly says he left VOA to join OSS.
claims.match_notes: Published with qualification and excluded from high-confidence default employer analytics until the personnel file confirms the transition.

claims.claim_text: Vincenzo Vacirca directed the New York newspaper La Strada in 1937.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Italian Foreign Ministry archival inventory identifies him as director of La Strada in New York in 1937.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence rare-name match consistent with his documented Italian American antifascist press work.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly dated prewar employment; not shown to be the immediate predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: Preserved as earlier employment and not substituted for the closer 1942 VOA affiliation.

claims.claim_text: Anthony J. Vaiksnoras studied at and graduated from the Cleveland School of Art in 1942 before U.S. Army service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Enamel Arts Foundation profile supplies the scholarship, graduation and Army sequence; the official Army occupation code independently aligns with art training.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence rare-name match corroborated by the protected Army identifier and aligned historical occupation category.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before Army entry; student status is not employment and is not claimed as immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Student status remains separate from employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Anthony S Vaivada is high-confidence matched to the Chicago Lithuanian newspaper editor who entered the U.S. Army in 1942 and served in counterintelligence.

claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact name, middle initial, Chicago journalism and documented 1942 Army chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources provide a coherent prewar-employment and wartime-service sequence but not the exact OSS assignment date.
claims.match_notes: Later intelligence work is used only for identity and wartime-pathway context.
